court: In the High Court of Madras†
case_number: W.P. Crl.(MD). No. 2725 of 2026 and W.M.P. Crl.(MD) No. 655 and 656 of 2026
advocates: For Petitioner : Mr. S. Sarvagan Prabhu
For R-1 and R 2 : Mr. A.S. Abul Kalaam Azad Government Advocate (Crl.side)
For R 4 : Mr. B. Ramanathan Additional Government Pleader
judgment_text:
Prayer : Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, praying this Court to issue a writ of certiorarified Mandamus, to call for the records pertaining to the impugned proceedings issued by the second respondent herein in his proceedings in C. No. 32/H1PS/2026 dated 1-5-2026 and quash the same as illegal and consequently direct the 1 and 2 respondents herein to grant permission to conduct the Chithira Pournami Urchava Vizha festival of Sri. Selva Vinayagar and Sri. Devi Karumaariyamman Temple located at Survey No. 1883/24 (old Survey No. 1750/B) situated at Narivilampatty, Kambiliampatty Village, Dindigul District, which is going to be conducted on 10-5-2026 to 14-5-2026 within the time that may be stipulated by this Court.

The Order of the Court was delivered by

S. Srimathy, J.:— The present Writ Petition is filed for Mandamus, to quash the impugned proceedings issued by the second respondent in C. No. 32/H1PS/2026, dated 1-5-2026 and consequently to direct respondents 1 and 2 to grant permission to conduct the Chithira Pournami Urchava Vizha festival of Sri. Selva Vinayagar and Sri. Devi Karumaariyamman Temple, located at Survey No. 1883/24 (old Survey No. 1750/B), situated at Narivilampatty, Kambiliampatty Village, Dindigul District, which is to be conducted from 10-5-2026 to 14-5-2026.

2. Through the impugned proceedings, dated 1-5-2026, the respondents refused to grant permission, citing that there is a dispute between two groups.

3. The petitioner states that he is collecting Thalaikattu Vari from some of the community people. However, the third respondent insisted that he would also pay Thalaikattu Vari. There is a restriction to collect Thalaikattu Vari only from certain people.

4. The learned government advocate (Crl. Side) submitted that the said issue cannot be considered in this Writ Petition. Further submitted that the petitioner may be restrained from collecting Thalaikattu Vari from their own community people also.

5. Based on the said submission, this Court is inclined to quash the impugned order dated 1-5-2026. Accordingly, this Writ Petition is allowed. The petitioner is restrained from collecting Thalaikattu Vari from the third respondent as well as from any person while conducting the festival for this year. In future, regarding Thalaikattu Vari, the petitioner is at liberty to approach the competent Civil Court to resolve the issue and the petitioner is at further liberty to collect donations alone to conduct the festival.

6. With the above direction, this Writ Petition is allowed. Consequently, the connected Miscellaneous Petitions are closed. No costs.
